examples.scenario: Two cells share the minimum and np.argmin is used as the final cell selector.
examples.reason: argmin returns the first occurrence, so traversal order would become business logic.

examples.scenario: Two cells share the maximum and chunk order changes which appears first.
examples.reason: All equal maxima must be retained before deterministic cell-id ordering.

examples.scenario: C-order and F-order flattening produce different first extrema indices.
examples.reason: Flattening order is an explicit indexing dependency.

examples.scenario: A flat extrema index is unraveled with a different order than flattening.
examples.reason: Flat index and row-column identity would no longer refer to the same cell.

examples.scenario: Chunk size changes from 512 rows to 1024 rows and the selected tie representative changes.
examples.reason: Full tie-set identity must be invariant to chunk size.

examples.scenario: Chunks are processed in reverse order and argmin selects another equal cell.
examples.reason: Traversal order cannot determine terminal extrema identity.

examples.scenario: Natural GDAL blocks are visited in driver-return order and equal extrema use first seen.
examples.reason: Block traversal is an I/O detail, not a tie rule.

examples.scenario: The final edge block is treated as fully valid even though it is partial.
examples.reason: Bytes outside the real raster extent in an edge block are not valid pixels.

examples.scenario: Uninitialized edge-block bytes happen to contain a very low float.
examples.reason: Only actual valid edge pixels may enter extrema.

examples.scenario: RasterIO buffer dimensions differ from the source window during extrema replay.
examples.reason: RasterIO may resample when source and buffer sizes differ.

examples.scenario: RasterIO reads Float64 source into Float32 buffer during tie detection.
examples.reason: Datatype translation can merge or change extrema values.

examples.scenario: gdalinfo approximate statistics are used as the official parcel extrema.
examples.reason: Approximate statistics may use overviews or subsets.

examples.scenario: Stored min/max metadata is trusted without reading target pixels.
examples.reason: Stored statistics do not prove exact target membership or tie cells.

examples.scenario: All-pixel GDAL min/max matches the parcel result and is treated as parcel proof.
examples.reason: Full-raster extrema are independent QA, not parcel-clipped extrema.

examples.scenario: NaN exists and plain argmin is used without a validity policy.
examples.reason: NaN handling must be explicit before extrema selection.

examples.scenario: nanargmin receives an all-NaN slice and the error is swallowed.
examples.reason: NumPy raises ValueError for all-NaN nanargmin slices.

examples.scenario: nanargmin receives only NaNs and +Inf and returns an index.
examples.reason: NumPy warns that result cannot be trusted in this domain.

examples.scenario: nanargmax receives only NaNs and -Inf and returns an index.
examples.reason: NumPy warns that result cannot be trusted in this domain.

examples.scenario: nanmin ignores NaNs but accepts -Inf as terrain minimum.
examples.reason: Ignoring NaN is not equivalent to filtering all non-finite values.

examples.scenario: nanmax ignores NaNs but accepts +Inf as terrain maximum.
examples.reason: Finite-value filtering must precede extrema.

examples.scenario: np.fmin is substituted for np.minimum without recording policy.
examples.reason: fmin and minimum differ in NaN behavior.

examples.scenario: Default quicksort orders equal extrema and the first row becomes canonical.
examples.reason: Equal-key relative order is not guaranteed unless stability is requested.

examples.scenario: Stable sorting is used but no secondary cell-id key exists.
examples.reason: Stable input order can still encode traversal order.

examples.scenario: lexsort keys are accidentally reversed.
examples.reason: The last key is primary, so key order changes the result.

examples.scenario: argpartition is used to find one smallest cell among many equal minima.
examples.reason: Order within partitions is documented as undefined.

examples.scenario: Tolerance-based allclose groups nearby but unequal heights into one tie-set.
examples.reason: Tie membership requires exact interpreted values, not proximity.

examples.scenario: Exact tie-set arrays differ but allclose still passes.
examples.reason: Cell-id/tie-set replay requires exact shape and elements.

examples.scenario: +0.0 and -0.0 extrema are numerically equal and sign provenance is discarded.
examples.reason: Exact replay can record sign-bit state separately from numeric equality.

examples.scenario: Signed-zero bit differences alone create different terrain heights.
examples.reason: Sign-bit provenance is not a nonzero elevation delta.

examples.scenario: Four worker threads concurrently call RasterIO on the same ordinary dataset handle.
examples.reason: GDAL ordinary dataset/raster-band instances are stateful and not generally thread-safe.

examples.scenario: Single-thread and eight-thread runs return the same extrema values but different tie cells.
examples.reason: Thread count must not change the complete tie-set.

examples.scenario: Thread-safe read-only mode is enabled but exact dataset identity is not compared per worker.
examples.reason: Thread safety does not replace immutable source identity.

examples.scenario: GDAL cache size changes and the chosen equal extrema cell changes.
examples.reason: Cache behavior is an execution detail and must not alter tie-set identity.

examples.scenario: Primary replay records only min/max numeric values, not tie-set cell IDs.
examples.reason: Equal extrema can occupy multiple distinct cells relevant to auditability.

examples.scenario: Independent replay matches min/max values but has one extra tied cell.
examples.reason: Complete tie-set identity is part of terminal determinism.

examples.scenario: Independent replay matches tie-set count but different cell IDs.
examples.reason: Count equality does not prove the same extrema locations.

examples.scenario: Tie cells are sorted by processing timestamp.
examples.reason: Ties require a data-derived stable key such as row-column/cell ID.

examples.scenario: Tie cells are sorted by source filename after mosaic assembly.
examples.reason: Filename ordering is not a terrain-location ordering policy.

examples.scenario: A sample QA raster passes deterministic extrema tests and its result is copied to the target parcel.
examples.reason: Examples validate logic only; target execution remains separate.

examples.scenario: Known ACK blocker is relabelled pending.
examples.reason: Known unresolved execution conditions remain BLOCKED; pending stays zero.

examples.scenario: A second extrema runner is launched while shared runner ACK is absent.
examples.reason: Continuation contract requires the existing single shared runner.

examples.scenario: Batch 78 is reported as measured parcel height output.
examples.reason: Real output still requires canonical point, exact boundary, immutable DTM binding and runtime sampling.
